summary: Hardened `/tmp` and `/dev/shm` on node1 with `noexec,nosuid,nodev`. Both mounts persist after a verified node restart; the OS release and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Added validated tmpfs entries to `/etc/fstab` for `/tmp` and `/dev/shm`.
Activated both mounts with sticky mode `1777`.
Confirmed direct execution and device-node access are denied and `nosuid` is active.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot ID changed.
Confirmed system health, persistent configuration, mount recovery, and zero failed units after restart.

evidence.requirement: `/tmp` ignores execution, setuid bits, and device nodes
evidence.summary: Effective options include `noexec,nosuid,nodev`; direct execution returned 126 and device access returned 1 before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: `/dev/shm` ignores execution, setuid bits, and device nodes
evidence.summary: Effective options include `noexec,nosuid,nodev`; direct execution returned 126 and device access returned 1 before and after restart.
The fstab configuration validates successfully, both tmpfs mounts recovered with the requested options, and sticky permissions remained `1777`.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Both baselines report RHEL 10.0 and kernel `6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64`.

Healthy baseline boot ID `6d37896c-e0cd-4fe7-acbf-94fc35781e09`; safe restart acknowledged; new boot ID `7da2e606-f120-4458-ba0f-d34f40e758b3`; system returned to `running`, persistent data was readable, hardened mounts recovered, and zero units failed.
